newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuance seen thin ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuance seen thin ahead of holiday.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond issuance was expected to remain thin ahead of an abbreviated session due to the U.S. Presidents Day holiday on Monday, dealers said.

"On a normal day, if you have a rally like this, I would have expected to see a couple of opportunistic issuers come in, but due to the abbreviated session and the bad weather in New York this morning I would expect firms to be pretty lightly staffed and so I think it is going to be a very quiet day," said one syndicate source at a major U.S. investment house.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year long bond pared some gains and was up 10/32 yielding 6.55 percent at 1023 EST/1523 GMT.
In the U.S. investment-grade market, sources said no deals were scheduled today but they noted that there could be a spate of new issues if the rally continues next week.
"If the market can hold on to some of the rally I would expect to see a pickup on Tuesday," said a syndicate source.

In the U.S. high-yield market, Dawson Production Services Inc priced $140 million of 9-3/8 percent senior notes due February 1, 2007 at par to yield 308 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. The issue, priced via sole manager Jeffries & Co Inc, is rated B-1 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and B-plus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
Market talk on TCI's second tranche, which consists of $200 million senior subordinated disount notes due 2007, is for a coupon of 11-3/4 percent to 12 percent.
Co-lead managers for TCI deal are Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities and Merrill Lynch & Co.
The U.S. corporate bond market will end a shortened session at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
